title: Rural Credit Decline and Alternatives for Producers
seoTitle: Rural Credit Falls: Alternatives for Producers Emerge
subtitle: Disbursements decline, default rates rise, and Banco do Nordeste offers renegotiation
excerpt: Plano Safra disbursements fell by almost 30% in the first quarter, while rural default reached 8.8%.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In the first three months of Plano Safra, disbursements through traditional rural credit lines fell by almost 30% compared to the same period of the previous season, raising concerns among producers already facing high default rates.

Plano Safra Disbursements Register Sharp Decline

Between July and September, the funds released totaled R$ 80 billion, a drop of almost 30% compared to the previous cycle, and the number of contracts fell from 717,000 to 555,000. This reduction directly impacts the availability of resources for operating costs and investments on properties.

Rural Default Reaches 8.8% in First Quarter

Data from Serasa Experian indicates that rural default reached 8.8% in the first quarter of 2026, a 1.2 percentage point increase compared to the same period in 2025. The indicator considers debts overdue for more than 180 days contracted with agribusiness companies.

Warning for New Credit Contracts

Victor Cardoso, commercial head at fintech Agree, highlights that in a scenario of increased financial pressure, taking on new credit without analyzing existing commitments can jeopardize future cash flow. He recommends consolidating debts, evaluating projected cash generation, and observing the concentration of maturities before seeking new resources.

Debt Renegotiation with Banco do Nordeste

Provisional Measure 1,376/2026 authorizes the renegotiation of over 117,000 credit operations in states served by Banco do Nordeste. In Sergipe, more than 3,000 producers, responsible for 3,300 operations, can join by November 12. Conditions include a payment term of up to ten years and a grace period of one year for the start of principal payment.

Practical Tips for Producers

Before contracting new credit, producers should:

  • Map all existing financial obligations;
  • Identify concentrated maturity periods;
  • Verify if terms are compatible with expected revenue generation;
  • Consider alternatives such as consortiums or insurance, which can reduce the need for immediate resources.
Additionally, those who already have debts can contact a Banco do Nordeste branch or use digital channels, such as the BNB portal or WhatsApp (85) 4020-0004, to initiate renegotiation.

With information from Globo, Agrolink, Infonet.
